body:
Started looking into this, but not sure how it should be handled.  I'm seeing the same behavior for `[b]`, combined `[b]` and `[i]`, and `[code]` tags.  Using `[font_size=32]` instead of `[font size=32]` works as expected.

It looks like bold, italic, and code tags are basically pointing to separate bold/italic/mono fonts, which can be overridden for the `RichTextLabel`, along with sizes for each.  So `[font]` and `[i]`/`[b]`/`[code]` tags specify a full font + size to be used, rather than changing a single property of the current font.  `[font_size]` seems to be more of an override of just the size property of the current font.

If we wanted to have `[i]`/`[b]`/`[code]` keep the current font size, it looks like we might be able to check with `_find_font(current)` to see if a font was already specified, and keep it's size (haven't tested yet though), just not sure if the behavior of these tags (and corresponding theme overrides) should be changed.
